status: Clang failures independently reproduced through GNU Make; exact underlying mechanism unresolved
scope: Diagnostic runs, excluded from baseline/candidate timing acceptance.

windows_host.WHEAQuery: No matching events returned for preceding 14 days
windows_host.Note: Host metadata and lack of WHEA events do not establish or rule out hardware instability.

findings: Five of six independent unmodified Linux6.12 GNU Make clean builds passed with identical vmlinux/bzImage hashes. The sixth failed while Clang19 parsed net/ethtool/linkinfo.c: stack smashing detected, frontend exit134/SIGABRT; GNU Make exited2. Openmktr was absent from these reference builds.

A further full WSL comparison failed in baseline warmup2, with Clang19 exit139 in both net/ipv6/addrconf.c preprocessing and drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-core.c code generation. No measured pair completed; all failed evidence is retained.

672 standalone compiles passed, including saved preprocessed shmem input and original addrconf/hid-core/linkinfo commands against the exact generated headers. Every repeated input produced one consistent object hash. Transience remains unexplained.
The recorded 64MB soft/hard stack limits and lack of cgroup OOM events do not identify a cure or a hardware cause. Host WHEA queries returned no events; this is not proof of hardware health.

Package verification found no checksum changes in Clang18/19, libclang-cpp, libLLVM or libc6. The LLVM19 image reported missing documentation files only. Compiler/library content corruption was not found by these checks.
The independent failure excludes attribution of all compiler faults solely to Openmktr. Hardware, WSL and compiler causes are not distinguished by the present evidence.
No runtime code, binary, kernel source contents or kernel optimization flags were changed in response to the crashes.
